Customer (Chris Murray): Can you explain how the equalization plan works out my monthly amount?
Agent (Naledi Nkosi): Hi Chris Murray, Naledi Nkosi here — let me pull that up.
Customer (Chris Murray): If the point of this plan is predictable payments, why does it keep moving?

Agent (Naledi Nkosi): To recap: the adjustment stands, it can be split over two payments, and your file is flagged for a call before the next change.
Customer (Chris Murray): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Naledi Nkosi): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Customer (Brian Wilson): I need to close my account at the old address and set up payments for the new one.
Agent (Nomsa Khumalo): Hi Brian Wilson, Nomsa Khumalo here — let me pull that up.
Customer (Brian Wilson): Do I need to be home for anyone to come out, or can this be done remotely?
Agent (Nomsa Khumalo): No problem, I can help with that.
Agent (Nomsa Khumalo): Can you give me the account number from your bill, or the service address and the name on the account?

Customer (Brian Wilson): What's the actual turnaround time between the stop and the start?
Agent (Nomsa Khumalo): What date do you need the stop to take effect?
Customer (Brian Wilson): The last day of the month. That's when we hand the keys back.
Agent (Nomsa Khumalo): Is the new address in one of our service areas?
Customer (Brian Wilson): Yes, it's still in Leduc County.
Agent (Nomsa Khumalo): Is the email on your account still current, for the confirmations?

Agent (Nomsa Khumalo): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Customer (Brian Wilson): So is this actually getting fixed today?
Agent (Nomsa Khumalo): I've submitted the request, but a technician visit is required to activate the new address's meter and the earliest slot is a few days out — I've flagged it as a move-in priority, but I can't guarantee same-day activation.
Customer (Brian Wilson): So I might be without gas when I move in?
Agent (Nomsa Khumalo): Possibly for a day or two. The new meter needs a technician to turn it on, and the earliest slot is a few days out.
Customer (Brian Wilson): Can you move it up?
Agent (Nomsa Khumalo): I've marked it as a move-in priority, and if a slot opens you'll get a call.
Agent (Nomsa Khumalo): To recap: the stop is booked, the new meter needs a technician visit, and you're on the priority list for an earlier slot.
Customer (Brian Wilson): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Nomsa Khumalo): Thanks for bearing with me. Everything's noted on your file, and you'll hear back as I said.

Customer (David Thompson): You charged me far more in fees than the gas actually cost. That can't be right.
Agent (Vusi Molefe): Hi David Thompson, Vusi Molefe here — let me pull that up.
Customer (David Thompson): Can you actually break down where every line item on this bill comes from?
Agent (Vusi Molefe): Thanks for bearing with us on this. Let me go through the bill with you properly.
Agent (Vusi Molefe): Before I go into the account, can you confirm the service address and the account holder's name?
Customer (David Thompson): Yes, same address as always, and the account's under my name.
Customer (David Thompson): This isn't the first time — I feel like I'm being charged fees just for having an account.
Agent (Vusi Molefe): Which line items are you disputing?
Customer (David Thompson): The distribution charge and the fixed charge. They're bigger than the gas.
Agent (Vusi Molefe): Have you raised this with us before?
Customer (David Thompson): Once before, and I was told it's just how the bill works.
Agent (Vusi Molefe): Would a line-by-line breakdown by email help?
Customer (David Thompson): Yes, I want to see where every dollar comes from.
Agent (Vusi Molefe): Let me take a look. I've reviewed the itemized charges line by line against metered usage and the current distribution rate schedule.
Agent (Vusi Molefe): Alright, I can see exactly what's going on here.
Agent (Vusi Molefe): The distribution charge and the fixed daily charge are set by the AUC for your rate class, so they apply even when the meter reads zero.
Customer (David Thompson): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Vusi Molefe): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Customer (David Thompson): So is this actually getting fixed today?
Agent (Vusi Molefe): The distribution and fixed charges you're seeing are billed under the AUC-approved rate schedule regardless of how much gas you actually use that month — I can explain the structure, but I don't have the authority to waive a regulated charge.
Customer (David Thompson): So there's nothing you can do?
Agent (Vusi Molefe): I can't waive a regulated charge. I can send the dispute to a billing specialist so every line is checked, not just explained.
Customer (David Thompson): How long will that take?
Agent (Vusi Molefe): You'll get a call with the outcome within five business days.
Agent (Vusi Molefe): To recap: the regulated charges stand, a billing specialist is checking each line, and you'll hear back within five business days.
Customer (David Thompson): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Vusi Molefe): Thanks for bearing with me. Everything's noted on your file, and you'll hear back as I said.

Agent (Kagiso Radebe): Hi Tyler Ross, Kagiso Radebe here — let me pull that up.

Agent (Kagiso Radebe): I've added an access note so the reader calls ahead.

Customer (Tyler Ross): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
